What comes up in Maroubra

3 conditions, and each one is handled differently

Every site is scoped on the day. The table describes how these jobs generally go in this area. Your block may not match it, which is the reason for looking at it first.

Knockdown with no usable side access

The common Maroubra constraint, and the thing that sets the programme.

How it is handled
Smaller plant or hand demolition, with material carried out to the kerb and loaded there rather than at the work face.
What does it
Mini excavator, hand tools, tippers staged at the street.

Weathered coastal cement sheet

Eaves, roofing and wall sheeting that decades of salt air have broken down.

How it is handled
Condition assessed before anything is touched, because weathered sheeting may have to be handled as friable rather than bonded.
What does it
Licensed asbestos removalists, licence class set by the condition rather than the material.

Freestanding houses

Single and double storey brick, brick veneer, fibro and timber. The era matters more than the material, because anything built before 1990 carries a hazardous materials assumption until it is tested.

How it is handled
Hazardous materials removed and cleared first, services disconnected in writing, then the structure taken down and the material separated as it falls.
What does it
Excavator with a demolition grapple, sized to the side access rather than to the house. Zero tail swing where the work runs hard against a boundary.

Maroubra

What shapes the work on these blocks

  • Tight blocks with little or no side access Which pushes work towards smaller plant, hand demolition and material carried out rather than loaded where it falls.
  • Coastal weathering on older stock Salt air breaks cement sheet down, and weathered material is assessed before it is touched.
  • Street parking pressure Which decides what vehicle can stand and how many loads the job takes.
  • High land value and a high redevelopment rate Knockdown rebuilds and dual occupancy on blocks with neighbours close on both sides.

In Maroubra the block and the street are both constraints. Where a side gap will not take a machine, material is carried out to the kerb; where the street will not take a truck and dog, the same volume goes out in far more tipper loads. Both are settled before the quote.

Maroubra questions

What people ask before we start

There is no side access at all. Can the job still be done?
Usually, with a different method: smaller plant, hand demolition where it is needed, and material carried out to the kerb. It is slower and it is priced that way rather than discovered on day one.
Does coastal weathering change how asbestos is handled?
It can. Badly weathered cement sheet may have to be treated as friable rather than bonded, which means a higher licence class, tighter controls and air monitoring. That assessment is made on site before anything is disturbed.
There is no side access at all. Can the job still be done?
Usually, with a different method. Smaller plant, hand demolition where it is needed, and material carried out to the kerb rather than loaded where it falls. It is slower and it is priced that way.
Is Max licensed for the asbestos removal itself?
Max holds the demolition licence, AD214737. The asbestos removal is carried out by licensed asbestos removalists, and the air monitoring and clearance by an independent licensed assessor. The whole pathway is managed as one job so you are not coordinating three contractors.
